slot.brief: Projectile given range and maximum height; solve the two trajectory equations to find launch speed and angle of projection.

stem: A projectile is launched from level ground and lands at the same level. Its range is $60$ m and its maximum height is $20$ m. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, its launch speed and angle of projection are

verdicts.working: From H = u_y²/(2g), u_y = 20 m s⁻¹. Flight time = 2u_y/g = 4 s, so u_x = 60/4 = 15 m s⁻¹. Thus speed = 25 m s⁻¹ and angle = tan⁻¹(20/15) ≈ 53.1°.

working:
$H=\dfrac{u_y^2}{2g}\Rightarrow u_y=20$ m s$^{-1}$.
$T=\dfrac{2u_y}{g}=4$ s; hence $u_x=\dfrac{R}{T}=15$ m s$^{-1}$.
$u=\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}=25$ m s$^{-1}$; $\theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{20}{15}\right)=53.1^\circ$.

Independent check: From H = u_y²/(2g), u_y = 20 m s⁻¹. Flight time = 2u_y/g = 4 s, so u_x = 60/4 = 15 m s⁻¹. Thus speed = 25 m s⁻¹ and angle = tan⁻¹(20/15) ≈ 53.1°.
solution:
From $H=\dfrac{u_y^2}{2g}$, $u_y=\sqrt{2gH}=20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. Thus $T=\dfrac{2u_y}{g}=4\,\text{s}$ and $u_x=\dfrac{R}{T}=15\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.\\
$$u=\sqrt{u_x^2+u_y^2}=25\,\text{m s}^{-1},\qquad \theta=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{u_y}{u_x}\right)=53.1^\circ.$$
